correctness.rationale: In T(a,b,c), a directed 3-cycle consists of exactly one vertex from each of the three transitive blocks. S(x,y)=[x=y or no third vertex making a cyclic triple] consequently defines the blocks in FO^3, and S(x,y)∧R(x,y) is their internal total order. Recursive path-length tests reuse only three variable symbols and separate every finite block size; a directed cycle of representatives records their cyclic order. Every vertex has both an in-neighbor and out-neighbor, giving an indefinite two-pebble Duplicator strategy. Burnside gives [binom(N-1,2)+2*1_(3|N)]/3, and rigid internal orders give N!*binom(N-1,2)/3 labelled objects. Independently re-enumerated cyclic composition orbits for N=3..13 and obtained the formula. These finite tests corroborate, not replace, the unrestricted-depth pebble/formula arguments.
residual_risks: Definition of variable reuse requires local alpha-renaming with capture avoidance; scrutinized for the three-variable path recurrence.
No outside completeness or formula-size complexity claims.

value.rationale: An exact expressive-power boundary for a natural tournament substitution family, distinguishing unrestricted-depth FO^2 from FO^3 and classifying all theory types. The recoverable cyclic block order is a structural lemma applicable to other tournament logic constructions; the nontrivial k=3 threshold is not merely a formula-renaming artifact.
